pr_body:
Introduces a command to manually set urgency, as well as rendering of urgent views, sending the IPC event, removing urgency one second after focus, and matching urgent views via criteria.

To test, run something like `swaymsg [class="Firefox"] urgent enable`.

Try it with Firefox on a different workspace too, and notice the swaybar indicator working.

Note that urgency is not yet implemented when xwayland views request it, nor when a view requests focus (depending on the value of `focus_on_window_activation`). I feel like that's out of scope for this PR.

Closes #2258.

I also had a look at `focus_on_window_activation` but I think some changes would need to be made in wlroots (eg. a `request_activate` event).

EDIT: Instructions for testing xwayland urgency hint:

* Use a terminal that supports urgent on bell (eg. urxvt with `URxvt.urgentOnBell: true` in ~/.Xdefaults)
* `sleep 2 && echo -ne "\a"`, then focus away while the sleep is happening - terminal will become urgent
* `swaymsg urgent deny` to deny the view the ability to set itself as urgent
* `sleep 2 && echo -ne "\a"`, then focus away while the sleep is happening - terminal will not become urgent because it's denied

issue_context.title: Proposal: `urgent enable|disable` command
issue_context.body:
You would execute it with criteria:

* `[app_id="foo"] urgent enable`
* `[mark="foo"] urgent disable`

An example use case would be a chat program which doesn't support urgency or requesting focus but provides desktop notifications. Your notification daemon could, upon receiving a notification from this chat program, execute `swaymsg [some criteria] urgent enable`.

Another example is having a background script monitoring your GitHub notifications or email inbox for new messages, then when it gets a result it sets an appropriate browser window to urgent. If the notifications/emails are read from another location then the script can run `urgent disable` to clear the urgency.

Another example is configuring your shell to mark the window as urgent when it completes a long running command. If your terminal supports "urgent on bell", you can do this already by echoing a bell character, but using a sway command would work for all terminals. However, this would require the shell to determine its container ID so it can use it in the criteria, and I'm not sure how you'd do that.

Lastly, it would simply be useful to test the urgency implementation.
comments: At first, I thought this would let you ignore urgency from windows matching a criteria, which sounded coolio.

I don't see why we couldn't do that too. I used the terms enable and disable to fit with the fullscreen and floating commands. If you wanted to keep that consistency then we could have `urgent {enable,disable,allow,deny}` where allow and deny controls whether the view can request urgency itself. Or you could not be consistent and have `urgent {on,off,enable,disable}` but I prefer the first option.
